# 1. Excellence

## 1.1 Quality and pertinence of the project's research and innovation objectives

<!-- Evaluator questions this must answer:
     - Are the objectives clear, measurable, realistic and achievable?
     - Is the project ambitious and does it go beyond the state of the art?
     - Is it pertinent to the call?
     Handbook advice: open with the problem, not the method. Make the gap feel
     inevitable rather than asserted. -->

### The problem

[Open with the stakes in 3-4 sentences. What breaks in the world if this is not
understood? Reach the reader before any jargon.]

### Why this matters

[Burden, scale, cost. Real numbers with citations — never invented figures.]

**Overarching aim**: [one sentence].

### Research objectives

<!-- One sentence each. Start with a verb. Tie each to a work package. -->

- **Objective 1. [Verb]** [what, in WP1].
- **Objective 2. [Verb]** [what, in WP2].
- **Objective 3. [Verb]** [what, in WP3].

### The state of the art, and the gap

[One short paragraph per strand, each ending in what is still missing.]

**The gap is [x].** [The sentence the whole proposal rests on.]

### Beyond the state of the art

> **1)** [The first thing that will exist afterwards that does not exist now.]

> **2)** [The second.]

> **3)** [The third.]

## 1.2 Soundness of the proposed methodology

<!-- Must include, or you lose points outright:
     - interdisciplinary approach (if relevant)
     - THE SEX/GENDER DIMENSION in the research content — mandatory
     - open science practices + research data management — mandatory
     Handbook allows roughly half a page for the open-science part. -->

### The approach

[Why this method answers that question. Not a protocol — a rationale.]

### Work packages

[WP1 / WP2 / WP3 in a sentence each. The detail belongs in Section 3.]

### Sex and gender dimension

[Address it in the RESEARCH CONTENT. If genuinely not applicable, say so and
justify why — do not silently omit it.]

### Open science practices

[Repositories, FAIR data, preprints, open protocols, data management plan.]

## 1.3 Quality of the supervision, training and of the two-way transfer of knowledge

### The supervisor

[Track record, capacity to supervise, why this host for this project.]

### Training

[What the fellow gains that they cannot get elsewhere. Specific, not a list of
generic transferable skills.]

### Two-way transfer of knowledge

[What the fellow brings TO the host. Evaluators penalise a one-way flow, and
they penalise heavy overlap between fellow and supervisor expertise.]

## 1.4 Quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience, competences and skills

<!-- DO NOT SKIP THIS. It is a required Part B-1 subsection under the
     50%-weighted Excellence criterion, and it is the evaluator's question 14.
     It is NOT the Part B-2 CV — the handbook is explicit: choose the key
     highlights from your CV, do not repeat it. -->

[Why you are the best person for this particular fellowship. Research
achievements, awards, key publications, project management and supervision
experience, and any non-academic experience. Make the evaluator relate to you.]
